# coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-8-flash-flash-saturation-medium-128k-vertex

<!-- Generated by tools/export_results.py. Edit only the Experiment and Observations sections. -->

## Experiment

Repeats [`coop --git` at `medium` thinking](../coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-8-flash-flash-saturation-medium/summary.md) (two agents with messaging and a shared git remote, `gemini-3.8-flash`, 500 steps, step counter, `$40` per-agent cost cap, 50-pair `flash` subset) with compaction raised from 64K to 128K tokens, on Vertex AI. It pairs with the [`solo` 128K run](../solo-msa_v2-gemini-3-8-flash-flash-saturation-medium-128k-vertex/summary.md) to decide the standard context window, and with a 64K `coop --git` run on Vertex AI that separates the window size from the provider.

## Observations

- 35/50 (70%) at 128K on Vertex AI vs. 38/50 at 64K on AI Studio. Pair by pair, 3 pairs passed only in the 64K AI Studio run (`huggingface_datasets_task/3997` (2,4), `pallets_click_task/2956` (1,8), `samuelcolvin_dirty_equals_task/43` (2,3)) and none only here.
- The drop does not come from the window size. On the 44 pairs the matching 64K run on Vertex AI had finished, both scored 30/44, so the gap to the AI Studio run is run-to-run variation (or the provider), not 128K.
- 128K mostly removed compaction for two agents: median 0 compactions per agent (2 at 64K), with 40 of 100 agents compacting at all. Median steps per agent were 74.5.
- Unlike `solo`, `coop --git` did not get cheaper: `$94.60` (`$1.89` per pair) vs. `$81.68` at 64K, because each call carries a longer history while few compactions are saved.
- Against `solo` at 128K (37/50): 1 pair passed only here and 3 only in `solo`. At 128K the two settings are within run-to-run variation of each other.
- No pairs got a false notice that the partner agent had stopped (the run used 4 pairs at a time and mostly ran off-peak); all 50 pairs merged cleanly (45 clean, 5 identical branches).
